newsitem.title: USA: Order may close "Baby Richard" case.
newsitem.headline: Order may close "Baby Richard" case.

text.p: The Illinois Supreme Court on Monday overturned an order that could have reopened the case of "Baby Richard," who was forcibly returned to his natural parents after living with adoptive parents the first four years of his life.
The court, without comment, ordered Cook County Circuit Court Judge Gay-Lloyd Lott to drop an order he had issued last week to have the boy's current home life investigated.

The high court also ordered the judge to allow the boy's natural mother Daniella Kirchner to drop her efforts to regain her legal standing as the boy's mother -- something she gave up when she put him up for adoption shortly after his birth six years ago.

Monday's decision may be the final act in the saga which drew international attention in 1995 as the boy, whose real name is Danny, was taken in tears from his adoptive parents and returned to the natural parents he had never known.

The turn-over was the result of an Illinois Supreme Court ruling in favour of the boy's natural father, Czech-born Otakar Kirchner. When the child was born he was out of the country and the couple was not married.

The boy's mother told Kirchner the baby had died. About two months later he found out the boy was alive and began a legal battle to recover him. The couple later married and took the child to live with them after the adoptive parents surrendered him.

The Kirchners later separated but the boy remained with Daniella Kirchner by mutual agreement. The Kirchners said they wanted to revoke her original consent to have her newborn son put up for adoption as a precautionary measure, in case something happened to his father.

She later tried to drop her request for a revocation but the judge whose order was reversed on Monday had refused to allow her to do that and told child welfare authorities to investigate the Kirchner home.
